full_judgment:
21. The writ-petitioners have relied upon the conduct of the authority stating that since the writ respondents who are responsible for issuing licence sold the trawlers, which were used as fishing trawlers and they purchased the trawlers on the understanding that they would be given necessary licence for fishing and accordingly, they installed fishing gears and equipment's and obtained certificates of inspection and registrations, which according to them had accrued rights to get licence. These are mere assumptions and presumptions on hypothesis, which do not confer any right or interest under any established doctrine or principle. These presumptions, even if there be any, are not obligatory. A presumption is a rule that a particular inference shall be drawn from particular facts whoever proved them. The writ petitioners having not pleaded in support of the claim and in the absence of established precedents or rules from which it may be inferred, the writ petitioners are not authorised by law to get licence, to speak the least, under any theory of law. 

 94. In judicial review of administrative actions, the Court has to start with the presumption of regularity of the official act and the burden of proof is on the person who alleges the contrary. Whenever a power is given by statute to an authority, whatever may be fairly regarded as incidental to or consequential upon things authorized by legislature should not be declared ultra vires (AG vs Great Eastern Rly Co (1880) 5 APP case 473). The Courts should not compel a public authority by issuing a writ of mandamus to perform an act which are within its domain.
